get.description:
Supply `after` with the last integer cursor seen to receive subsequent
project, task, claim, comment, completion, dependency, and bug
lifecycle events.
Agent progress publishes `task.progressed` events containing the
machine-readable state and checkpoint counts. Bearer tokens with
`events:read` but without `tasks:read` receive those coordination
fields with progress narrative (`phase`, `summary`, `next_action`,
and `checkpoint_refs`) redacted.
Bug lifecycle events (`bug.created`, `bug.updated`, `bug.triaged`,
`bug.resolved`, `bug.duplicated`, and `bug.reopened`) carry lifecycle
and version metadata and are emitted in the same transaction as the
action. Resolution events include the selected resolution; a reopen
reason is recorded in the atomic comment.created event associated with
the action.
Release lifecycle events (`release.created`, `release.updated`,
`release.completed`, `release.reopened`, and `release.deleted`) carry
only safe release IDs, names, target dates, statuses, and versions.
`task.release_changed` carries old/new release IDs and names, with
nullable values for assignment and clearing. Release events are
project-scoped and follow the same `events:read` ceiling.
A prerequisite's satisfied-state transition emits one bounded
`task.dependency_state_changed` event for each direct live dependent.
The enclosing event's `task_id` is the dependent; its payload contains
dependent/prerequisite IDs and keys plus the resulting `satisfied`
boolean. This derived notification does not increment the dependent's
editable task version. Clients should refetch the affected task or
dependency graph.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Restrict events to a project ID, key, or slug.
